factProposals.value: Grid heat maps of work orders (counts per 50 m to 2 km square, with a breakdown by work type), filtered by type, date range and status, as GeoJSON or an SVG image.
Only work orders with coordinates can be mapped: those created from a GIS asset, or citizen requests with a map pin. Work orders with only a freeform location are counted as unmapped.
factProposals.evidence: server/heatMaps.js (matchingWorkOrders); tests/heatMaps.test.js (add up, citizen's map pin)

factProposals.value: City planners and staff use heat maps through an API client with the heatmaps:read scope.
Heat maps are never public and contain only per-cell counts, because a cell with one work order can point to one citizen's report; the SVG is served as a sandboxed image.
heat_map_log records every heat map generation attempt with who asked, format, parameters, start and finish times, duration, outcome, error and result counts.
Which cell size, filters and output the planners actually want, and whether the city GIS will load the GeoJSON as delivered, are not known.

decisions.statement: Count work orders without coordinates as unmapped rather than leaving them out silently.
decisions.rationale: A heat map must say how much of the data it shows; geocoding addresses would need an outside service and account.

decisions.statement: Use one fixed square grid anchored at Herriman's latitude.
decisions.rationale: Maps from different runs and filters line up and can be compared cell by cell.

decisions.statement: Provide GeoJSON for a street-map view in the city's GIS instead of drawing a street map.
decisions.rationale: A street map needs an outside tile service with its own terms and account.

decisions.statement: Refuse maps over 5,000 cells or 250,000 grid squares with advice.
decisions.rationale: Such maps are unreadable and slow; refusing clearly is better than producing them.

decisions.statement: Return no map if its log row cannot be written.
decisions.rationale: The Trust criterion: every heat map generation is logged.

limitations.statement: Neighbouring work orders near a cell edge can be counted in different cells; there is no smoothing.
limitations.evidence: tests/heatMaps.test.js (a larger cell size merges nearby points)

limitations.statement: The SVG image has no street map or place names.
Citizen map pins are used for placement but are not copied onto the work order itself.
Refused (unauthorized) heat map requests are recorded in the audit trail and request log, not in heat_map_log, because nothing was generated.
There is no planner-facing page; heat maps are requested through the API.
